correctness.rationale: The proof exactly characterizes a valid one-step inverse at each start. Two adjacent valid starts necessarily give the same parent, so distinct parents inject into an independent set of a path with \(n-1\) vertices, yielding \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor\). The period-four complement-pair word attains the bound, and fixed-point-freeness guarantees pairwise distinct parents. The finite verifier independently matches forward and inverse channel implementations over twelve exhaustive cases and checks the construction through \(n=100\) for five even alphabet sizes. The computation is corroborative; the universal conclusion rests on the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: The maximum inverse degree is the exact worst-case uncoded list ambiguity of the one-error reverse-complement channel, a natural incidence invariant relevant to decoding and list behavior. It also gives a sharp even-length contrast to the foundational odd-length fixed-parent uniqueness phenomenon: at duplication length \(2\), distinct-parent ambiguity can grow linearly and its exact coefficient is \(1/2\). The result holds for every even alphabet and every source length \(n\ge2\), rather than for a narrow finite parameter slice.
